standard_prerequisites.name: Quasi-finiteness is preserved by composition, and the characterization of purity by impurities
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Morphisms, label morphisms-lemma-composition-quasi-finite (proof line 4921); Same chapter flat.tex, definition labelled definition-pure and the characterization following it (proof line 4924)
standard_prerequisites.use: The first shows that an impurity over the base change with the composite morphism quasi-finite gives an impurity over the base, and the characterization turns the non existence of impurities into purity.

core_obligations: Translate an impurity: given an impurity of the pulled back module over the new base with the morphism quasi-finite at the point, compose with the quasi-finite base change to obtain an impurity of the original module, the composite still being quasi-finite at the point (proof lines 4916-4921).
Conclude from the characterization of purity by the non existence of such impurities (proof lines 4922-4924).
proof_roadmap: Translation of an impurity along the composite (proof lines 4916-4921).
Conclusion from the purity characterization (proof lines 4922-4924).
difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that purity along a fibre is preserved by a base change which is quasi-finite at the point (statement lines 4907-4914, tag 05L2-adjacent). The proof is short but complete: an impurity of the pulled back module with the morphism quasi-finite composes with the quasi-finite base change to give an impurity of the original module, and the characterization of purity by the non existence of impurities gives the conclusion. The translation of the impurity is the substance, so the claim is H2.
